quest.title: The Dead Past is the Living Present
quest.description: After the sands have settled, you and the others bid farewell to the ancient grounds and return to the Akademiya...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x60, Mora x31125, Guide to Admonition x5, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahhh~! That was good. Feels like everything's finally wrapped up now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Life is all about these moments when you can finally relax and hang out with good friends after a job well done... And also those desserts Cyno got — they were really good! Paimon definitely needs more of those in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then let's come back again sometime.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you three have anything planned for the rest of the day?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If not... Would you come somewhere with me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, where are we going?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's a secret for now. Wouldn't want to spoil the surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Okay, I think I can guess where you're talking about... It'll definitely be a nice surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, now Paimon's curious! Come on, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Grandfather...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You, Sethos, and the other members of the Temple bid farewell to Bamoun.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: In the great hall, people gather around the coffin to pay their respects. The atmosphere is solemn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Sethos... You'll get through this.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I know, I just... I'll miss him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I am so sorry for your loss.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I guess you were prepared for this. It's been a long time coming, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Yeah. He's been on death's door for a very long time now. I think it was only through sheer willpower that he managed to hold on to this point.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: ...At least he was able to see this chapter come to a close before he passed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's next for you?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Per my grandfather's last wishes, the Temple of Silence should submit to whoever possesses the largest number of Hermanubis fragments. That entitles you to be our new leader, Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But that's never going to work, as I'm sure you realize. I'm the General Mahamatra. I am needed back at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I did foresee this possibility, and I gave it some thought. The fact is, I know next to nothing about the staff, records, and environment here. As such, I am ill-suited to be your leader.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sethos, I believe the honor should go to you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Were it not for this duel, or indeed if you had other intentions... The Ba Fragments would most likely be in your hands by now. I'm sure Bamoun never meant for anyone but you to be his successor.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: You really think so?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I do.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Still, I didn't think Bamoun looked very surprised by the final result. Perhaps he had an inkling that this would be the way things end.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Well, in any case, since the Ba Fragments are with me now, I guess I can call the shots.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sethos, I would like you to succeed Bamoun as the new leader of the Temple of Silence. You are more suited to the role than I, and I have complete faith that you will be an excellent leader. Just think of it as doing me a favor.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: But doesn't that render everything that we've been through up to now meaningless?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No, it doesn't. This experience has allowed us to become friends, which means that the Akademiya and the Temple of Silence will become partners once more.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's a much bigger deal than you might think, Sethos. You said yourself, times have changed. You have to believe that things can change for the better here at the Temple, too.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: ...I will try. To be honest, I couldn't have asked for a better outcome.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Actually, part of me wonders whether Bamoun's intention from the very beginning was just to create enough pressure to force us towards a duel.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That way, no matter who won, one of us would have to surrender our Ba Fragment, and the power of Hermanubis would be concentrated in one single person.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Had you won, the Temple of Silence would have doubled its strength.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And were I to win, he correctly anticipated that I wouldn't suddenly drop everything to become the leader of the Temple, much less integrate the Temple into the Akademiya by force.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: He knew that the Temple's future would depend not just on the guidance of Hermanubis, but the support of the Akademiya too. So he made it his responsibility to ensure his successor would be free from the burdens of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: His plan meant that whoever ended up succeeding him, they would have an easier time interacting with the Akademiya. With one single letter, he lured out the Professor... No matter what happened after that, it would result in a net benefit to the Temple.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: ...And here I thought the General Mahamatra wouldn't care for all these trivial details.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: You're absolutely right. Grandfather and I considered this from every angle. We had to find a way to mend our relationship with the Akademiya... In that sense, the Rite of Duels was just a means to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Thank you for everything, Cyno. As a gesture of our gratitude, to those that you and Lesser Lord Kusanali deem worthy, I will grant the honor of access to the Temple of Silence for their pursuit of knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: The Temple of Silence has a wealth of information on King Deshret's civilization, more than any other organization in existence today. In times when you need information that only we can provide, we will be here to support you.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: But you must be exceedingly careful with your selection of candidates, lest you lead humanity to repeat the same mistakes.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: By the way, Tighnari, my grandfather was so happy to see you. You are a descendant of the Valuka Shuna, and we are the heirs to the will of Hermanubis.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: The story goes that King Deshret chose the sage Hermanubis from among the Tighnarians, and appointed him as his familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: He went on to fight many valiant battles with his Tighnarian companions. They always stood by each other, from the founding of the Temple of Silence to the fall of Tulaytullah.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: The Tighnarians who left Tulaytullah joined their human counterparts in the rainforest. A few centuries later, when some of the group returned to the desert, many of the Tighnarians chose to stay, and put down roots in the rainforest.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: In all likelihood, those were your ancestors.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: How fascinating... My father once mentioned that I was named after the Tighnarians, but I never knew that my forebears had such a history with the Temple of Silence.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I like this story.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, has anyone seen Cyrus?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Ah yes, Cyrus... You'll probably find him in my grandfather's room. He wouldn't show it in front of me, but I think he still has many fond memories of my grandfather.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If it's true that you and your grandfather really planned for everything to turn out this way, then I guess he didn't really resent Cyrus as much as he appeared to.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Heh, who knows? Perhaps all of us — you, me, and Cyrus — were all just pawns in my grandfather's plan to set things straight. He was awful like that.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Someone's got to make the decisions when history is at a crossroads.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I will make a detailed report on all of this to Lesser Lord Kusanali, and arrange for an official delegation from the Akademiya to come and meet you in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm sure you'll have lots to attend to in the days ahead. But once things return to normal, please come and visit the rainforest again. You should stay for a few days this time, and start to build some relationships.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If we're going to work together, both sides have to get to know one another better.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Alright, well... Bye for now, everyone. I'll be seeing you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See you soon! Come hang out with us anytime!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Best of luck to you, Sethos.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: What were you thinking, gallivanting off into the desert alone, at your age!? What if you'd kicked the bucket, hmm? You told not a soul what you were up to, designated nobody to handle your affairs, and left everyone scrambling frantically to try and figure out how on earth to clean up the colossal mess you'd made!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh please, will you stop your yelling! What other choice did I have?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: What do you mean, what other choice!? Do you mean to tell me that after all your years of learning — and sagehood, no less — the only idea you could conjure up in that white-haired walnut of yours was to shoot off into the unknown like some hot-headed 20-year-old adventurer?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: A one-man suicide mission, hmm? That's the best idea that one of the finest minds of a generation could come up with, is it? ...It astounds me that you survived the journey, and you're lucky that Bamoun didn't finish you off when you arrived!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Alright, alright! Honestly, the way you're going off on me, it's like you wished you'd been there to lend him a hand... Does it mean nothing to you that I am your colleague and former classmate?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Phew... *sigh* I've got nothing more to say. What's the point of berating an old bag of bones...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: What do you mean, bag of bones? I'm a flesh-and-blood hero who, despite his old age, saved our General Mahamatra from being stripped of his powers!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...Okay look... *sigh* Fine, I admit, I was in the wrong... How can I make it up to you? What about... a month's work at the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Hmph, one month? Try three!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari's master is really laying into Cyrus... Uh, let's give them a wide berth...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, we're too young to get involved...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Professor brought this on himself. Don't pay any attention to him.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Wow, I haven't seen Master get this riled up in a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The last time he chewed someone out like this must have been back when I was still a student...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I think I'll go around and update everyone, tell them the situation's resolved. Want to come with me?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We can go for dinner afterwards, my treat. You in?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Makes sense. I'm in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's coming too! Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hey, Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Huh? Well, look who we have here... Would you mind explaining to me what has been going on these past few days? I heard you all ran off into the desert and got embroiled in a major catastrophe?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: All taken care of.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: That does NOT answer my question! How could you be so careless? That goes for you as well! Yes, and you two!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: When you run into problems, you really ought to ask for help, you know. I've been around the block, don't you think it would have made sense to involve me? And let's not forget, I know the desert like the back of my hand...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Now would not be a good time to attempt to argue with Faruzan.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mhm!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: It's not the first time that I've had to talk to you about this sort of thing, either. You need to learn that there are times when the right thing to do is get a more experienced member of staff involved. Do I make myself clear? Because if you don't, I...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: (Collei, please do something!)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (...! He's giving me the signal! Alright, guess it's time to play my ace-in-the-hole...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Um, say, Madame Faruzan, I can see you're pretty upset, but, uh, I was just wondering... Remember that time you offered to give me a tour of the Akademiya? Does that offer still stand?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ah... Wait, did I hear that right? Collei, you remember? Wonderful! Well, of course the offer still stands! Come on, Madame Faruzan will show you around the old classrooms...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Poor Collei, getting dragged off like that... Also, check out Faruzan acting like some sort of official Akademiya tour guide...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ahem, Collei! Cup!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh? What? ...O—Oh, right!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmm? What do you mean, "cup"? You need a cup? I can get you a cup.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, it's nothing, just Master's way of reminding me to stay hydrated while I'm out and about, hehe, heh...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's code for "let's reconvene at the cafe." Tighnari and I used it while we were in school, and it's become something of a family tradition now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's kinda fun.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Two people left. Let's bring them along too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Am I hallucinating? Or do I see Kaveh and Alhaitham engaged in diligent studying?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We're just re-organizing all the books we used. Look, there's a whole mountain of them!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There's no rush. Nobody reads these books anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: My sincere thanks to you both.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes, with your help, we resolved the issue rather swiftly and painlessly. And the outcome was better than we could have hoped for.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cyno informs Alhaitham and Kaveh of everything that happened in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I see. The Temple of Silence resorted to rather unique means of self-preservation. It explains how they managed to remain hidden for so many years.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And it sounds like they managed to preserve a whole load of ancient documents as well... I'd love to go check those out if I ever had the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That day will come. The Temple of Silence is a hugely important organization, and we'll be sure to maintain good relations with them in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Now, as a token of my appreciation, I'd like to treat everyone to coffee.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Sounds good.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah, sounds great, um... Although, after the last few days, I don't know if I can handle another coffee. But I can just order something else.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sure, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...And then, {NICKNAME} just pounced on their opponent, and knocked 'em right out cold!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then there was Tighnari — he put up an amazing fight, too! We ended up winning all three bouts!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Whoa... Part of me wishes I'd been there to see it, but... I'd have been biting my nails off worrying about you guys...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: A truly edifying account of the events. Bereft of detail, but it has livened up the room all the same.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, Paimon included all the juicy details! {NICKNAME} just pounced, and then waved their sword like this! Then spun around! And blocked!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Despite winning three bouts in a row, you still ceded the position of leader to him. That's very dignified of you, Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Of course. Being dignified comes with being a true champion.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I got to be a champion too, for once. I've not sparred much with desert folk before. It was a pretty unique experience.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The venue was pretty impressive too. A very ceremonial affair.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, huge place, it felt like something right out of an epic poem! Imagine this, it was like there was...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Maybe save that one for later, Paimon. Dessert's here.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone enjoys each other's company and the General Mahamatra's generosity. The shockwaves left by the Temple of Silence gradually fade away.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I think that'll do me for today.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Shall we stop off at the House of Daena again before heading home? We should probably finish putting all those books back.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: My thoughts exactly. See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I should get going as well. See you all later! Make sure you get some good rest tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I need to go say thanks to the Corps of Thirty for their help. Also, Sir Naphis said he wanted to introduce me to some of the Akademiya's work processes... So I gotta dash too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Collei's come a long way. She's much more confident at dealing with other people these days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone's a work in progress. You never stop learning.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yeah, true.

talks.objective: Go to the place Cyno mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Been a while since I last made my way up here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, look at this place... We're so high up!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Need any help?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Hahaha... As you wish.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: It's a nice spot, isn't it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a great view! We're so high up, we can see for miles.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: #{NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Turn around.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...It's beautiful.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: This is my secret base. Somewhere I only bring my best friends.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: When I was a student, I used to slip away and climb up here all the time, just to clear my head. I was quite young then, and hadn't made too many friends yet.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Back then, I had a lot of the same questions that Sethos was asking: Who am I? Why do I have this power? And what should I be fighting for?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Our gifts help us to find our rightful place in the world. That was my experience, and I'm sure Sethos will figure things out in his own time, too.

choices.text: As long as Hermanubis's power endures...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: You two really are like brothers.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I feel the same way.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Of course. I see no need to be humble when it comes to the facts.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I still remember one time when we came up here to chat and do our homework. Cyno accidentally dropped a fruit... Luckily, he has fast reflexes, so he caught it just in time.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: That was the one and only time. Nothing will ever slip through my fingers again.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ah, those were good times. I kinda miss the student life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know, Paimon really shouldn't be able to imagine Cyno doing something like that. But for some strange reason, the mental image is coming through clear as day...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Then make it stop.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Hm? There's somebody there...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...It's Professor Cyrus.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You guys carry on without me. I'll be right back.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Okay.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Hey! You're not supposed to jump down! Be careful!

choices.text: You will remain inextricably linked to the Temple of Silence.
I am actually a tree-climbing champion!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh my days, I can't believe how stupid I look in this one...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Professor. What are you muttering to yourself about?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Cyno! Just the man I'm looking for! Guess what I found in some old notebooks?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Some old photos?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Can you believe it? This notebook was just sitting in a pile of odds and ends in the sages' office. I must have forgotten to take it with me, and no one's touched it since. It was still right there.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: I was at the Akademiya earlier to discuss my workload with Naphis. I swung by the old office to have a look around, and just happened across it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: How time flies. Look how tiny you are in this picture! Still a kid...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You look quite young yourself in that one.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ah, it's this one! I remember that, Lisa took it, didn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Yep, looks like her work alright. Who else could've found just the right angle to make me look so unbelievably hideous...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And this one. Looks like we're both dozing off.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hah, cheeky girl... Taking secret photos of us without our knowledge...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Is there something you'd like to say to me, Professor?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Like what? Like... "These are good photos, aren't they"...?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...Hey. At moments like this, I... I hardly know where to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...I can't pretend I'm a good person. Bamoun had every reason to despise me, and... Well, so do you, if you feel the same way.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't be ridiculous, you old codger.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ugh. Is that not what you wanted me to say!?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...I dreamt of that place many times after leaving the desert. Sometimes, I'd dream that I was doing research with them again, and other times, I'd dream of the day they saved my life.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: It was... one of the happiest times of my life. We all learned so much from one another.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: You've matured so much over the years, Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Since you're my professor, I should save you some face by not calling you out on all the non-answers you just gave... So, I will do the right thing and keep my mouth shut.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hmph, good thinking! Take your own advice next time!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Seriously, why bully an old man like me? I thought heroes were supposed to be gracious...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hey, wait... Huh, how did I not notice this one earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Lisa strikes again. Just how many did she take?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Look how cute you were when you were little. I remember how well-mannered you were back then, too...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yeah, and look how serious and professional you used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh, I can't compete with you anymore... First you get better than me at the deadpan jokes, and now, you're besting me at those little quips, too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't say that. I still have a lot of respect for you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hmph. That's more like it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...Hey, what would you say to meeting up with Lisa again sometime?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'd like that. Let's find a time and pay her a visit in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll add it to my schedule. Let's go next week.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Wait no! Next week is the tomato-growing competition. I have got to beat Zaha Hadi!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Or you could find a real hobby, Professor.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: ...Grandfather, we did it. We achieved what we set out to do.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: From this day on, the Temple of Silence has the chance to work with the Akademiya once more. Real change, real opportunities... They are now within our grasp.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: You'd better start packing your things. Report for work first thing tomorrow morning — I'll be waiting for you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: What about my allowance? Oh, and is lunch covered? How about dinner?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Don't push your luck... Let's not forget who is compensating whom here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hey, a man's got to eat! Help me figure out something for lunch at least? I'm counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...*sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: The people of the desert are stubborn folk, fiercely loyal to their heritage, even if it means suffering years of hardship and pain. You said this yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: But why did you feel the need to go this far? You never were the fearsome leader you made yourself out to be, Bamoun.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Being stubborn and unyielding is bound to send you to an early grave. Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: (Did you see, Grandfather? Cyno chose me to succeed you as leader of the Temple of Silence. I will now serve in his stead.)

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: (It's still early days, and I can't say that I know him that well yet. But after that battle, I now understand why he came here with a whole group of friends.)

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: (Companionship means to trust and be trusted. Just like Cyno and his friends, we too will fight side by side and support each other in times of trouble.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: (All these years, I've felt like I'm still young, I still have lots to look forward to in life.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: (But now... I suddenly feel...)

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: (I too have grown old, Bamoun, just like you.)

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: (I should have asked him to come help out at work much earlier. That would have kept him out of trouble, and avoided this whole debacle...)

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: (If Naphis thinks he's getting a single day of free labor from me, he's got another thing coming!)
